# Design

The visual rules for 4GHz. The approved source is the Visual Direction page in Confluence (GHZ-4); the colors, shapes, and fonts live in [`design/visual/tokens.json`](design/visual/tokens.json), and `pnpm tokens` generates the front matter above and `src/tokens.css` from it. `pnpm check` fails when either is out of date, and `design/visual/check-colors.ps1` checks contrast and color vision distance for every pair.

## Personality

Tidy, glanceable, slightly futuristic. The app is opened for a few seconds to check what is due and tick it off. The interface stays quiet and precise; the futuristic feel comes from details rather than effects: a monospaced face for codes, tabular figures for countdowns that tick every second, hairline borders, and a mark of three stepped bars, one per game, like a signal indicator. No glow, gradients, neon, or shadows.

## Color

- Cool neutrals with one accent per game. The selected game's accent (`data-game` on `<html>`) colors main actions, the selected tab, switches, radios, focus, notices, and the all-done highlight.
- Each game keeps its own color everywhere (`genshin`, `hsr`, `zzz`). In the calendar a game's dot sits in a fixed position under the date, so position, not color alone, says which game it is. Elsewhere a small dot sits beside the game's name.
- Warnings use the fixed `warning` color and an icon, never the accent, so they never read as a notice.
- Components use token names only, never raw colors.

## Themes

- Light and dark follow Windows (`prefers-color-scheme`); there is no in-app theme switch.
- Windows contrast themes (`forced-colors: active`) let system colors win. Calendar dots are drawn as borders so they stay visible, and the all-done day keeps an outline from a transparent border that only contrast themes draw.
- Anything shown only by a fill keeps a system color in contrast themes: the radio dot and switch thumb are `CanvasText`, and the highlighted menu item is `Highlight` with `HighlightText`.
- Only token colors compile: `src/index.css` clears Tailwind's palette, so a class such as `bg-red-500` or `text-white` generates nothing.

## Typography

- Pretendard Variable for Korean and Latin text, including countdowns, with tabular figures.
- JetBrains Mono for codes, so they read clearly character by character.
- Both are SIL OFL 1.1 and bundled from the official files, unmodified; no font is loaded from a CDN. Their license texts are in the third-party notices.

## Shape and detail

- 6 px radius on controls and rows (`rounded-lg`), 4 px on calendar cells (`rounded-md`), 3 px on checkboxes (`rounded-sm`).
- Hairline borders (`border`) instead of shadows on rows and panels. Menus and dialogs float over content, so they use the control border (`border-input`), as in the approved preview. No shadows, blur, or glow anywhere.
- Hover and selected fills use `muted` (the hairline color); a hovered accent button changes to the accent text shade. Controls (checkboxes, radios, switches, select triggers) never sit on a `muted` fill, because their border falls below 3:1 there; rows that hold controls show hover and selection another way, such as the accent soft fill.
- The dialog overlay dims the page in both themes (`bg-foreground/20`, `bg-background/70` in dark).
- Notices carry a 3 px accent bar on the left; warnings carry the warning color and an icon.
- Links that open the browser end with an external-link arrow (↗), and only those.
- Focus is a 2 px accent outline in every theme, from one rule in `src/index.css`. Components never hide it (`outline-none`) or replace it with a ring, which is a box shadow that contrast themes remove; `pnpm check` enforces this.

## Components

shadcn/ui on Base UI (`src/components/ui`), generated by the shadcn CLI and changed only to apply these tokens and sizes. App components compose them and use Tailwind classes with the token names above.

## Window

- The app draws its own title bar: the header is the drag area, with the window buttons at its right end, sized and ordered like Windows' own (minimize, maximize or restore, close). The buttons are reachable by keyboard after Settings, and close turns red on hover as in Windows.
- Only the content below the header scrolls. Scrollbars are thin and use the `input` color on a transparent track; contrast themes keep the system scrollbar.
- In windows narrower than 768 px, Refresh and Settings show only their icons, with the text as the accessible name and tooltip, and the last-updated text moves to Settings > Data.
- Tradeoff of drawing the frame: the Windows 11 Snap Layouts flyout on the maximize button is not available. Win+arrow keys, Alt+F4, double-clicking the title bar, and dragging to a screen edge still work; Alt+Space and resizing from the window edges are checked by hand in acceptance testing.

## Calendar

- No boxed cells. A day shows one thing: the filled cell when every played game is done, or otherwise the dots of the games done, each in its game's fixed position, so position, not color alone, says which game it is. Today is a filled circle in the accent color (the system highlight in contrast themes); a day still being finalized has a dashed ring. Days of other months and days to come are muted. A past day with nothing done stays plain; its accessible name says which games were not done.
- The legend names the dots and the three day states in one line under the grid.

## Lists and countdowns

- Each schedule entry and code is a card of its own. Every card takes the accent on its border and a light fill on hover. A schedule entry with an announcement is a button that opens it, marked by an arrow at all times.
- Settings lists the sections for each game first and those for the whole app below a divider; there is no other line between the list and the content.
- Countdowns use units, not colons: "5일 18시간 07분 05초". Units below the largest keep two digits so the text keeps its width. Checklist groups show "초기화까지 …" under their title, and the exact time in a tooltip.
